discovery: Theoretical foundations of quantum computation and quantum simulation with trapped ions and neutral atoms

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Quantum optics / quantum information / atomic physics
motivation: Cirac and Zoller turned controlled atoms into a platform for quantum information. Their 1995 proposal of a quantum logic gate between trapped ions was the first realistic design for a scalable quantum computer. It set the direction for trapped-ion processors that now run high-fidelity algorithms. With Jaksch and others, they showed in 1998 that cold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. That proposal led directly to the observation of the superfluid-Mott insulator transition and began analog quantum simulation of many-body physics. Their proposals on quantum networks, quantum repeaters, atom-photon interfaces, Rydberg-mediated gates and lattice gauge theories have been confirmed by experiment again and again. Much of today's quantum computing, simulation and communication with atoms, ions and photons rests on concepts they introduced.
